== Research Notes ==

A possible identification concerns Benjamin Glasgow, Drapersfield merchant. Benjamin Glasgow and William Glasgow were mill partners and plaintiffs in the 1858 watercourse action. Benjamin had approached John Sloan about weir levels in 1856.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 22 July 1858, p.3; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390574459/ record]; Belfast News-Letter, 23 July 1858, p.4; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390575046/ record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain. The Drapersfield man was active after 1833. If the surgeon who died at New Orleans in 1833 was this Benjamin, the later mill partner was a different man; these are competing identifications, not one continuous life.

A possible identification concerns Benjamin Glasgow, Drapersfield merchant. Benjamin Glasgow, Esq., Drapersfield, Cookstown, was a contact for the auction of Eary House and lands from the estate of the late William Magee. The advertisement does not explicitly call Benjamin an executor.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 22 December 1869, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/388287498/ record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain. The Drapersfield man was active after 1833. If the surgeon who died at New Orleans in 1833 was this Benjamin, the later mill partner was a different man; these are competing identifications, not one continuous life.

A possible identification concerns Benjamin Glasgow, Drapersfield merchant. A contemporary July 1870 report credits Benjamin Glasgow of Drapersfield with granting use of a field for the 12 July Cookstown gathering. This postdates [[Glasgow-2059]]’s recorded death on 8 February 1870 and strongly supports a separate person.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 15 July 1870, p.4; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/387881589/ record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain. The Drapersfield man was active after 1833. If the surgeon who died at New Orleans in 1833 was this Benjamin, the later mill partner was a different man; these are competing identifications, not one continuous life.

A possible identification concerns Benjamin Glasgow, Drapersfield merchant. The named witness Benjamin Glasgow identifies the late Robert Glasgow as his father, says he managed his father’s mill from 1850, and dates Robert’s death to 1856. Benjamin’s evidence describes a companion as “witness’s uncle, Mr. Glasgow, sen.”; identification as William belongs to the separate case context, not this quotation.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 22 July 1858, p.3, Benjamin’s sworn testimony; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390574459/ record].</ref> Certain documentary father–son relationship; identification of Robert with [[Glasgow-2656]] or [[Glasgow-3941]] remains qualified. Counsel’s reference to Robert’s sons supports a qualified brother inference for co-plaintiff William. The uncle’s paternal or maternal side and all mothers are unstated. No parents are established for [[Glasgow-2058|John Glasgow]]. The identification remains uncertain. The Drapersfield man was active after 1833. If the surgeon who died at New Orleans in 1833 was this Benjamin, the later mill partner was a different man; these are competing identifications, not one continuous life.

A possible identification concerns Benjamin Glasgow, Drapersfield merchant. Benjamin Glasgow of Drapersfield, Cookstown, married Wilhelmina, eldest daughter of Richard Pike, Esq., of Beechgrove, Dungannon, at Dungannon on 16 February 1864.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 18 February 1864, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/387828785/ record].</ref> The original notice gives his wife and her father but no groom age or father. The identification remains uncertain. The Drapersfield man was active after 1833. If the surgeon who died at New Orleans in 1833 was this Benjamin, the later mill partner was a different man; these are competing identifications, not one continuous life.

A possible identification concerns Benjamin Glasgow, Drapersfield merchant. Margaret George Glasgow, eldest daughter of Benjamin Glasgow of Hull, formerly Drapersfield, Cookstown, married W. Brooke Broadbent, formerly Manchester, in New York on 5 October 1891.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 16 October 1891, p.1; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/388748472/ record].</ref> This directly bridges the father’s Hull and Drapersfield locations. The bride’s mother and age are unstated; W. is not expanded. The identification remains uncertain. The Drapersfield man was active after 1833. If the surgeon who died at New Orleans in 1833 was this Benjamin, the later mill partner was a different man; these are competing identifications, not one continuous life.

A possible identification concerns Benjamin Glasgow, surgeon of Vera Cruz and New Orleans. Benjamin Glasgow, surgeon, formerly of Vera Cruz, Mexico, died at New Orleans on 26 November last, according to a May 1834 notice. He was son of the late Robert Glasgow of Cookstown, County Tyrone. A Dublin notice repeats the surgeon, New Orleans and father details.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 20 May 1834, p. 3, Benjamin Glasgow death notice; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390554297/ record]; Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 23 May 1834, p. 4, Benjamin Glasgow death notice; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050049974/ record]; University of Glasgow Story, Benjamin Glasgow, Master of Surgery, graduation 1826; [https://universitystory.gla.ac.uk/people?search=&surname=Glas&forename=Benjamin record].</ref> 1833 is inferred from “last” in the 1834 publication; no age or mother is stated. Both notices concern one death, not independent witnesses. [[Glasgow-3412]] is a strong compatible surgery-graduate candidate, not a proved identity. The father was dead by 20 May 1834, distinct from the mill father who died in 1856. [[Glasgow-3941]] remains compatible by chronology only. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Benjamin Glasgow, surgeon of Vera Cruz and New Orleans. Benjamin Glasgow is listed under Masters in Surgery in a Glasgow University report stating that gentlemen from Ireland were admitted to degrees during the session.<ref>Freeman’s Journal, 7 May 1825, p.2, Glasgow University degrees; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050085983/ record]; Freeman’s Journal, 23 May 1834, p.4, surgeon death notice; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050049974/ record]; University of Glasgow Story, Benjamin Glasgow, indexed graduation 1826; [https://universitystory.gla.ac.uk/people?search=&surname=Glas&forename=Benjamin record].</ref> Strong compatible candidate [[Glasgow-3412]] and the Cookstown/New Orleans surgeon account; no father, hometown, age or overseas career appears here. The identification remains uncertain.
